s1.where: A full-screen prompt asking me to turn on notifications
s1.expectation: A start-up page asking me to turn on Messenger notifications, before I'm really in the app
s1.cue: The big bold title about turning on notifications and the bell picture

first_pass.why: It's a single question with a clear bold title and two buttons, so I know what it wants from me. I'm not lost.

s2.where: Main Messenger home screen with the chats list
s2.expectation: The main Chats list, the home of the app
s2.cue: The blue 'Chats' tab at the bottom. The 'messenger' logo at the top only tells me the app.

first_pass.why: The top only says 'messenger', which is just the app's name. The blue Chats tab at the bottom is what tells me where I am, but it's small and far away. In between there's a blue notifications banner, a row of story bubbles, a floating purple Meta AI blob and big blue 'Add friend' buttons all pulling at me, so I find the Chats tab last.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Chats' at the top where the logo is, and make the Chats tab stand out more. Fewer bright extras (banner, AI blob, Add friend buttons) on this screen.

test_cases.task: On the first screen scroll down two screens, pause, name where I am; then tap the middle and right bottom items and come back with the left.
test_cases.real_if: You have to hunt or guess to name the place after the pause.
test_cases.not_real_if: You can name it at once from what is on screen.
test_cases.what_happened: I scrolled the chat list down two screens and stopped. The top still only said 'messenger' and the blue banner was still there. What told me where I was is the little blue 'Chats' tab at the bottom, and I could name it straight away from that. When I tapped People and Notifications, the top changed to a big bold 'People' and 'Notifications', so those tabs name themselves at the top and Chats is the only one that doesn't. My taps were slow to register and I had to tap twice.

test_cases.task: Motion I noticed on this screen (not about knowing where I am).
test_cases.what_happened: On the Chats screen the purple Meta AI bubble stretched into an 'Ask Meta AI' pill by itself while I looked. That kind of movement pulls my attention, but it doesn't change knowing where I am.
test_cases.reason: About motion, not about knowing where I am.

s2.closing_comment: I can find where I am from the Chats tab, but the top should say 'Chats' like the other tabs say their names.

s3.where: A side menu panel slid over the home screen
s3.expectation: A side menu, not really a place
s3.cue: The list of menu items. The name at the top is the account, not a place.

first_pass.why: The name at the top, 'Ally Cooper', is the account name. It doesn't name a place. The list has no highlighted row, so I can't tell which part of the app I came from or am in. It's a menu sliding over something greyed out.
first_pass.solution: Give the panel a title like 'Menu', and highlight the row for the part of the app I'm in.

test_cases.task: Open the side panel from the first screen, read it, close with Back; open it again from the People tab and look again.
test_cases.real_if: The panel never names itself and never marks where you came from.
test_cases.not_real_if: Something on it tells you what it is and where you are.
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the panel from Chats. The top just says 'Ally Cooper' with a gear, then a list. No title, no row highlighted. I opened it again from People and it looked exactly the same, with no hint that I'd come from People. Back closed it fine.

s3.closing_comment: Still a menu with no name that forgets where I came from.

s4.where: A 'Subscriptions' sheet with a Meta logo
s4.expectation: Subscriptions, a page for paid plans

first_pass.why: The title says exactly what this is. The Meta logo makes me wonder if I've left Messenger, but the title is clear enough.

s5.where: A blue Facebook Plus 'free week' sales page
s5.expectation: An advert or sign-up page for Facebook Plus, maybe not Messenger at all
s5.cue: The big Facebook logo and 'Try Facebook Plus free for one week'

first_pass.why: It feels like I've been dropped into an advert. There's no Messenger name and no title naming a place, just a sales pitch, so I don't know whether I'm still in the app.
first_pass.solution: Show at the top that this is still Messenger, e.g. 'Messenger > Subscriptions', and give an obvious way back.

test_cases.task: Side panel > Subscriptions > second row > first 'View all benefits'; read the top each time; leave with the X.
test_cases.real_if: You cannot say which part of the app these pages belong to, or cannot find the way out.
test_cases.not_real_if: You can name where you are and leave without trouble.
test_cases.what_happened: Subscriptions opened as a sheet with 'Meta Account' small at the top and a bold 'Subscriptions' heading, so that's clear. The second row opened a page with a big 'Meta One' title. 'View all benefits' opened 'Try Meta One Core free for one month'. That's a pitch, but I knew I was in the subscription pages I'd just come through. Three X taps got me straight back, with no trouble. None of it says Messenger, but I could follow it.

s5.closing_comment: Easier than the pictures suggested: I could follow and leave, even if nothing says Messenger.
